states.openQuestionFromPhase2D1: DPOR vs. DOLI — which agency actually issues individual Journeyman/Master licenses?
states.resolution: RESOLVED — DPOR is the correct, real issuing authority for individual Journeyman/Master licenses. DOLI's real, confirmed role is limited to APPRENTICE registration only (before licensure), not issuing the Journeyman/Master license itself. This is now corroborated by multiple independent sources including a direct official DPOR regulatory document (A501-27TRADEREGS.pdf) covering Journeyman electrician licensing requirements directly. The one earlier secondary source claiming DOLI issues the licenses themselves is now assessed as inaccurate given the weight of corroborating evidence.
states.officialAuthority: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors / Tradesman Program

officialSources.title: Board for Contractors — Individual License and Certification Regulations

criticalFactsVerified.reciprocityJourneyman: CONFIRMED — real bilateral agreements with Kentucky (Journeyman+Master) and West Virginia (Journeyman+Master).
criticalFactsVerified.reciprocityMaster: CONFIRMED — real bilateral agreements with Kentucky, Maryland (MASTER ONLY, not Journeyman), and West Virginia.
criticalFactsVerified.qualifyingStatesByRank: CONFIRMED, rank-specific: Kentucky (both ranks), Maryland (Master only), West Virginia (both ranks). North Carolina's agreement is Contractor-specific, not an individual Journeyman/Master agreement.
criticalFactsVerified.examRequirement: CONFIRMED — reciprocal applicants still sit the Virginia-specific exam section; only the national portion is waived.
criticalFactsVerified.additionalPathway: CONFIRMED — Universal License Recognition (ULR) exists as a separate, broader pathway alongside the 3 named bilateral agreements.
criticalFactsVerified.issuingAuthority: RESOLVED this pass — DPOR, not DOLI, for the actual license.

states.openQuestionFromPhase2D1: Full scope of the Master-license reciprocity exclusion, and the exact qualifying-state list for Journeyman reciprocity.
states.resolution: RESOLVED — found a more directly on-point official source (DORA's own live Applications page, not just the general regulation text) that gives the complete, exact 14-state Journeyman list, independently corroborated by a separate secondary source that also states '14 specific states.' The Master exclusion is confirmed as a full, unconditional exclusion — the official Applications page's entire 'Electrician Licensure By Reciprocity' section addresses Journeyman only, with no Master pathway mentioned at all, consistent with the regulation text's unqualified statement.
states.officialAuthority: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA), Division of Professions and Occupations (DPO), State Electrical Board
states.licensingLevel: STATE — statewide license under Colorado Revised Statutes Title 12 Article 115

officialSources.title: Electrical Board: Applications and Forms
officialSources.authorityLevel: official-board (direct DORA/DPO application page — the most directly on-point source found for this state)

criticalFactsVerified.journeymanReciprocity: CONFIRMED — Colorado follows National Electrical Reciprocal Alliance (NERA) bylaws.
criticalFactsVerified.qualifyingStates: CONFIRMED, exact list of 14: Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming.
criticalFactsVerified.masterReciprocity: CONFIRMED, fully excluded — no Master pathway via reciprocity exists at all; the official Applications page's reciprocity section covers Journeyman exclusively.
criticalFactsVerified.examRequirement: CONFIRMED — no written exam required when NERA conditions are met.
criticalFactsVerified.eligibilityConditions: CONFIRMED — license must be current/active/good standing, obtained by state-administered examination (not grandfathering), and held at least 1 year.
criticalFactsVerified.fee: NOT independently confirmed against the official page's fee schedule this session — still Unknown.

states.decisionRationale: The single blocking gap from Phase 2D.1 (the exact qualifying-state list, previously contradicted between two secondary sources) is now resolved with high confidence via a direct, live DORA/DPO application page — the most authoritative and directly on-point source class possible, independently corroborated by a separate secondary source citing the same count (14 states). The Master exclusion — the most important content-integrity fact for this state — is confirmed unconditionally. Only the exact fee remains unresolved, a minor operational detail, not a fact whose absence would make the page inaccurate (it can be marked Unknown/pending per Rule 5's own standard).
